title: Encoding is not encryption
body:
Base64, hex and URL encoding only change how data is written, so it fits in text. Anyone can reverse them with no key. Encryption needs a secret key.

If a secret is only encoded, it is not protected at all.

Defenders: never treat encoding as protection; encrypt secrets or, better, keep them out of files and backups.

How to spot it: text made only of letters, digits, + and / that ends in = is probably base64; pairs of 0-9 and a-f are hex; %20-style groups are URL encoding. If a tool decodes it with no key, it was never encrypted.
